description:
At once captivating and haunting, playful and grotesque, Butoh is a form of Japanese dance theater that emerged from the traumas of war and a shifting cultural identity, recognized by a slow, unsettling state of movement. Also known as Japan’s dance of darkness, performers imagine their bodies as vessels between worlds, exploring transformation through contorted postures, and seeking understanding about life, death, and decay. 

Connecting with artists from Tokyo’s Butoh community, director Alisa Berger offers a trance-like meditation on the experimental art form for the short film GHOSTS – featuring performers Norihito Ishii, Tenko Ima, Seiji Tanaka, Yoshito Ohno, MUTSUMINEIRO, Yuri Nagaoka, Ooshikanosuke, Momoko Mei, Seisaku, and Kana Kitty. Capturing their distinct aesthetics and glacial choreography, Berger employs original music by German composer Simon Rummel, and intimate camera angles to carry the visual language of Butoh to film, drawing viewers to a sense of disquiet, and the liminal space where transformation takes place... read more at nowness.com
